prompt:
You receive 5 images. Image 1 is the LAYOUT SKETCH of the finished 1920x1080 game screen: a crude flat-colour blocking that fixes the exact composition - camera, horizon, wall and floor lines, and the position, size and outline of every object. Repaint image 1 into a finished painting: keep every line and every block exactly where it is and exactly as large as it is, paint each block as the object described below, do not move, enlarge, shrink, add or remove anything, and leave no flat colour areas or hard geometric edges. Images 2-4 are photos of the real place (geography, architecture, materials and real details to paint from; they are references only, do not copy their camera, cars, people, signs or weather). Image 5 is a finished background painting from our game: use it ONLY as the reference for the painting technique (brushwork, palette, edge softness, level of detail, line quality); do not copy anything from its scene.

Place: the back room of grandmother Mira's old garden outbuilding in the old village core of Čierna Voda (municipality Chorvátsky Grob, near Bratislava, Slovakia). Image 2 is a real narrow converted home workshop with shelves, workbenches and a small window in the end wall - use its lived-in density, but not its laminate floor, its machines, its ceiling lights or its modern plastic. Image 3 is a real old home workshop in an outbuilding: rough lime-plastered brick walls - the walls of this room. Image 4 is a real old bench with opened valve radios and measuring gear - the kind of low-voltage bench equipment on the workbench. Image 5 is our finished painting of the front room of this same building: paint this room in exactly its technique, with the same whitewashed brick walls, dark timber beam, worn pine floorboards, colours and warm light (its door, skis, shelves and suitcases belong to the front room, do not copy them). An invented interior, not a copy of any photo; no brands or labels from the photos.

Brief: the back room of the outbuilding, Mira's secret little workshop ZVON: a low-voltage bench apparatus, a panel with three shaped connectors, a large paper schematic, and a soft blue light in a round frame. It feels like a grandmother's tidy old hobby workshop with one strange, quietly humming device - wonder, not a laboratory. A sunny autumn afternoon on 29 October 2020: warm low sun comes through the small window on the right and draws a patch on the floor, warm light also falls in from the doorway to the front room just outside the picture on the left; the blue ring glows softly and tints the wall around it.

Camera: exactly as frontal and flat as image 5 - eye level, looking straight at ONE wall. The back wall is parallel to the picture and fills the picture from the left edge to the right edge; no side walls, no room corners, no doors or doorways, no walls or beams running into the depth. The camera is close to the wall, so the ceiling is NOT visible: only the heavy timber beam runs horizontally along the top edge (y 0-44). Keep this exact geometry from the sketch - the space above the shelf is short: the schematic at y 44-144 (4-13 % from the top) right under the beam, the long shelf board at y 252 (23 % from the top) running from the left picture edge to x 1218, the four interactive props in the top quarter of the picture on and right above that shelf, the workbench top at y 510 (47 %), the brass ring at y 120-390, the window at y 170-410, the skirting where the wall meets the floor at y 780 (72 %) across the whole width, and the floorboards from y 792 to the bottom edge.

What the sketch blocks are: the dark heavy timber beam along the top edge; the back wall is rough whitewashed lime plaster over brick with a patch of bare red brick lower right; a large sheet of yellowish paper pinned flat to the wall right under the beam: a hand-drawn schematic in blue and black ink in which lines connect a circle to a circle, a triangle to a triangle and a square to a square, with some circuit lines - no words, no digits; a long sturdy high oak wall shelf on black iron brackets from the left picture edge across the left two thirds of the wall; a small wooden box on the shelf; in the left corner under the end of the shelf a tall narrow old wooden cupboard with two panelled doors; under the shelf a long worn workbench standing against the wall: a grey isolated low-voltage bench power supply with two round analogue meters, a soldering station, a yellow multimeter, loose papers and notebooks, boxes of components; wooden crates and an old metal toolbox under the bench, against the wall; on the right the round light: a heavy brass ring frame on the wall, about a metre across, filled with a soft glowing blue light; a small old wooden cabinet under it against the wall; a small four-pane window with a sill showing Mira's sunny autumn garden (yellow vine leaves, warm light). Everything stands against the back wall and ends at the skirting line y 780.

Interactive props - each painted clearly inside its block, the same size as its block, easy to recognise at a glance:
1. the block of the layout sketch at x 120-240, y 150-250 of the 1920x1080 frame (6-12 % from the left, 14-23 % from the top): on the left end of the high shelf, the ZVON bench node: a small cradle of dark polished mahogany and brass with an empty round brass socket in the middle, made to hold a brass pocket-watch-sized chronometer, two brass terminal posts and a small glass fuse holder at the front with a visibly blackened, blown fuse; a cable runs down from it to the power supply on the bench.
2. the block of the layout sketch at x 425-545, y 150-250 of the 1920x1080 frame (22-28 % from the left, 14-23 % from the top): hung flat on the wall right above the shelf, under the schematic, a small dark wooden patch panel with three shaped sockets on the left (circle, triangle, square, top to bottom) and three on the right in a different order (square, circle, triangle), cream-coloured, with three loose patch cables (red, green, yellow) hanging from its lower edge.
3. the block of the layout sketch at x 730-850, y 150-250 of the 1920x1080 frame (38-44 % from the left, 14-23 % from the top): on the shelf, an old chipped orange enamel mug used as a pencil cup, with four pencils of different colours and a dried-out black felt marker sticking out.
4. the block of the layout sketch at x 1035-1155, y 150-250 of the 1920x1080 frame (54-60 % from the left, 14-23 % from the top): pinned flat to the wall right above the shelf, a hand-made yellow warning card with a red border, a red warning triangle at the top and three underlined lines of red handwriting below it (illegible scribble, no real letters).

Walkable floor: the band at x 90-1830, y 790-1015 of the 1920x1080 frame (5-95 % from the left, 73-94 % from the top) is the worn wide pine floorboards running left to right - one continuous floor, nothing stands or lies on it: no boxes, no crates, no cables, no rugs, no stools. Only the patches of warm light, a faint blue tint near the ring, soft shadows and a little dust. The floor continues to the left edge, towards the doorway back to the front room outside the picture (the area of the layout sketch at x 50-105, y 975-1045 of the 1920x1080 frame (3-5 % from the left, 90-97 % from the top)).
This room has no NPC zones.

Fiction rules: the ZVON node, the shaped connector panel, the schematic, the blue ring light and the warning card are invented props of a fictional device; no brand names, logos or readable labels on any equipment, box or paper; the meters show only tick marks. No people, no animals, no ceiling lamps.

The layout sketch is a blocking aid only: paint over all of it. Do NOT draw frames, borders, outlines or boxes around objects, and keep no flat colour block. The finished picture contains no UI, no captions, no text except what is asked for above, no watermark and no people or animals unless stated above.

Style: classic 1990s hand-painted adventure game background. Rich painterly brushwork, slightly exaggerated cartoon proportions with gently curved lines, warm late-afternoon sunlight, saturated but harmonious colours, soft dappled shadows under the trees.
